nodes.summary: Let $R$ and $S$ be commutative rings with $S$ an $R$-algebra, let $q$ be a prime ideal of $S$, and let $p$ be its preimage in $R$. Then $q$ is residue separable over $R$ if and only if the residue field $\kappa(q)$ is separable over the residue field $\kappa(p)$, for the algebra structure induced by the canonical local homomorphism $R_p \to S_q$ of localizations.
nodes.title: Residue separability, unfolded

nodes.summary: Let $R$ and $S$ be commutative rings with $S$ an $R$-algebra that is essentially of finite type, and let $q$ be a prime ideal of $S$ at which $S$ is unramified over $R$, that is, the localization $S_q$ is formally unramified over $R$. Then $q$ is residue separable over $R$.
nodes.title: Unramified primes are residue separable

nodes.summary: Let $R$ and $S$ be commutative rings with $S$ an $R$-algebra, let $q$ be a prime ideal of $S$, and let $p$ be its preimage in $R$. Then $q$ is residue separable over $R$ when the residue field $\kappa(q)$ is separable over the residue field $\kappa(p)$, for the algebra structure induced by the canonical local homomorphism $R_p \to S_q$ of localizations.
nodes.title: Residue separability at a prime

nodes.summary: Let $R$ and $S$ be commutative rings with $S$ an $R$-algebra, and let $q$ be a prime ideal of $S$. If $q$ is tamely ramified over $R$, then $q$ is residue separable over $R$.
nodes.title: Tame primes are residue separable

nodes.summary: Let $R$ and $S$ be commutative rings with $S$ an $R$-algebra that is finite as an $R$-module, and let $q$ be a prime ideal of $S$ whose residue field $\kappa(q)$ has characteristic $0$. Then $q$ is tamely ramified over $R$ if and only if $q$ is residue separable over $R$.
nodes.title: Tameness in residue characteristic zero

nodes.summary: Let $R$ and $S$ be commutative rings with $S$ an $R$-algebra, and let $q$ be a prime ideal of $S$. Then $q$ is tamely ramified over $R$ if and only if $q$ is residue separable over $R$ and the characteristic of the residue field $\kappa(q)$ does not divide the ramification index of $q$ over $R$.
nodes.title: Characterization of tame ramification

nodes.summary: Let $R$ and $S$ be commutative rings with $S$ an $R$-algebra, and let $q$ be a prime ideal of $S$. If $q$ is residue separable over $R$ and the characteristic of the residue field $\kappa(q)$ does not divide the ramification index of $q$ over $R$, then $q$ is tamely ramified over $R$.
nodes.title: Criterion for tame ramification

nodes.summary: Let $R$ and $S$ be commutative rings with $S$ an $R$-algebra that is essentially of finite type, and let $q$ be a prime ideal of $S$ at which $S$ is unramified over $R$, that is, the localization $S_q$ is formally unramified over $R$. Then $q$ is tamely ramified over $R$.
nodes.title: Unramified primes are tamely ramified

nodes.summary: Let $R$ and $S$ be commutative rings with $S$ an $R$-algebra, and let $q$ be a prime ideal of $S$. Then $q$ is *tamely ramified* over $R$ when $q$ is residue separable over $R$ and the characteristic of the residue field $\kappa(q)$ does not divide the ramification index of $q$ over $R$.
nodes.title: Tamely ramified prime

nodes.summary: Let $R$ and $S$ be commutative rings with $S$ an $R$-algebra, and let $q$ be a prime ideal of $S$ that is residue separable over $R$. Then $q$ is wildly ramified over $R$ if and only if the characteristic of the residue field $\kappa(q)$ divides the ramification index of $q$ over $R$.
nodes.title: Wild ramification under residue separability

nodes.summary: Let $R$ be a commutative ring, $S$ a commutative $R$-algebra and $q$ a prime ideal of $S$. Then $q$ is wildly ramified over $R$ if and only if $q$ is not tamely ramified over $R$.
nodes.title: Wild ramification is the failure of tame ramification

nodes.summary: Let $R$ be a commutative ring, $S$ a commutative $R$-algebra and $q$ a prime ideal of $S$ with residue field $\kappa(q)$. If the characteristic of $\kappa(q)$ divides the ramification index of $q$ over $R$, then $q$ is wildly ramified over $R$.
nodes.title: Divisibility of the ramification index forces wild ramification

nodes.summary: Let $R$ be a commutative ring, $S$ a commutative $R$-algebra, $q$ a prime ideal of $S$ and $p$ the preimage of $q$ in $R$. If the residue field extension $\kappa(p) \to \kappa(q)$ is not separable, then $q$ is wildly ramified over $R$.
nodes.title: An inseparable residue field extension forces wild ramification

nodes.summary: Let $R$ be a commutative ring, $S$ a commutative $R$-algebra and $q$ a prime ideal of $S$. Then $q$ is *wildly ramified* over $R$ if it is not tamely ramified over $R$.
nodes.title: Wildly ramified prime

nodes.summary: Let $R$ be a commutative ring, $S$ a commutative $R$-algebra and $q$ a prime ideal of $S$ with residue field $\kappa(q)$. If $q$ is tamely ramified over $R$, then the characteristic of $\kappa(q)$ does not divide the ramification index of $q$ over $R$.
nodes.title: The residue characteristic of a tame prime does not divide its ramification index

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
